label: paper; order not sent; CV call on our own streamed footage mapped to a live tennis market for timing (different sport); feed baseline 1 s is simulated (licensed feed not purchased)
assumed: assumed data: licensed feed/video not purchased; parameters measured
v2_label: v2 numbers are at the fast tier's own fills (frozen rule; no impact model beyond the copied print)
never_claim: We did not buy a licensed feed or licensed video, we have no camera at any court, and no live ATP/WTA data was used. The tier-0 trader is simulated; its timing and fill inputs are our measurements.
what: Capital capacity of the CV strategy at the simulated 1 s feed baseline (both stamp-lag readings, 20 seeds, two allocations of the stale depth) and of v2, from walking the measured live book with the capacity verifier's fixes (fills capped at the resting shares; linear extrapolation beyond 12,800 shares); grid of net cap x $/order cap x phi x coverage.

readings.lagcal: post hoc estimate: stamp lag 3.14 s (one-day inference)

grid.v2_size_map: deploy_frac = 0.5 x order_cap/$1k; match_cap = $3k x net_cap/100; phi_v2 = share of each copied print

conventions.capital: 3 x peak dollars locked, 4 h ex-ante lock per position (repo convention); peak_locked_close_usd locks each position until its market closes (payout available); peak_locked_resolution_usd until its match finishes
conventions.sharpe: daily calendar P&L, zero-filled, x sqrt(365)
conventions.roc: seed-mean $/day x 365 / seed-mean capital (roc_ann_pct_mean_of_seed_ratios = the first write-up's mean of per-seed ratios)
conventions.frontier: cells sorted by capital that earn more $/day than every cheaper cell
conventions.sharpe_halves: along the size path (net cap 50 -> 5,000 sh at $250/order for CV, $1k for v2), the capital where the seed-mean Sharpe reaches half the smallest size's, linear in log capital
conventions.seed_band: 2.5-97.5 % of the 20 per-seed values (model draws, not data uncertainty)
conventions.wrong_call_loss: loss_wrong_c = per-share loss implied by the fill price actually charged (clipped to [0.01, 0.99]); loss_wrong_model_c = the unclipped model value

definitions.inplay_usd: all in-play prints of the moneyline universe
definitions.w03_usd: all prints 0-3 s after a jump's ONSET (public tape, 1 s stamps)
definitions.w03_with_move_usd: with-move prints 0-3 s after a jump's ONSET: the market's own stale-taking volume; the onset print is the reprice, so this is the closest public-tape proxy for the pre-reprice window where our correct-call fills happen
definitions.fasttier_q_usd: the qualifying fast tier's prints 0-3 s after jump DETECTION (v2's causal bucket_c; detection can lag the onset by up to 10 s)

paragraph: Simulated at a 1 s licensed-feed baseline (assumed data: licensed feed/video not purchased; parameters measured; paper only, no order sent), the CV strategy has no capacity to speak of at the pre-registered 2.0 s stamp lag: its Sharpe is 2.7 in sample and 0.8 in the burned OOS even at the smallest size, and a 1 s feed already sits at its breakeven feed delay (1.01–1.09 s). Under the post hoc estimate of the stamp lag (3.14 s, a one-day inference; 95% interval 2.23–3.22 s), with 10 covered matches a day and half the stale depth, it runs up to about $28,000–$40,000 of capital in the burned OOS and $55,000–$73,000 in sample at Sharpe ≥ 4 (where its Sharpe has halved from the smallest size), earning about $32–$68/day and $94–$183/day there. The range brackets how we share the stale depth with the faster traders already there: the upper end gives our shares the best levels of the book, the lower end a pro-rata share of every level. Capital is 3 × peak dollars locked under a 4 h lock per position, which is about what locking each position until its market closes needs (0.94–1.10×). Every fill walks the measured live book and never takes more shares than were resting. Beyond the half-Sharpe size, impact and match risk take over: correct-call edge falls from 2.4¢ a share at the smallest size to 1.8¢ at 5,000-share positions with $1k orders, wrong calls cost 3.0¢ to 3.7¢ a share, and bigger net positions per match add outcome variance faster than edge. The P&L peaks at $339/day on $219,000 in sample (Sharpe 2.0, seed band −$95 to $896) and $177/day on $83,000 in the burned OOS (Sharpe 1.3); 5,000-share positions with $1k orders make −$73/day in the burned OOS. Covering every match with a book raises the half-Sharpe capital to $65,000–$97,000 (burned OOS) and $114,000–$165,000 (in sample). Just below the half-Sharpe size our notional is 0.22% of Polymarket's in-play tennis volume, and our correct-call notional is 5% of the with-move prints in the first 3 s after each jump's onset: small next to the market, not small next to the trading around each reprice. A central $167/day data licence is covered from about $65,000 in sample and from $77,000 in the burned OOS (Sharpe 1.3 there; at no size with the pro-rata allocation); covering every match, the camera-free deployment (licence plus L4 cloud GPUs, $291–$315 a day) breaks even from about $65,000 in sample and $117,000 in the burned OOS. Depth per match has been about flat (+0.6% a month over the last six months); volume grew through more listed matches, which is the coverage dial, not deeper books. As a sensitivity with no date attached, twice the depth per match would put the half-Sharpe capital at $59,000–$99,000. For comparison, v2 at the fast tier's own fills peaks in the burned OOS at $92/day on $23,000.
caveats: The CV strategy is a simulation: no licensed feed or video was bought, no camera is at any court, and the 1 s feed baseline is simulated. Its timing rests on an unmeasured stamp lag; the two readings bracket it and give very different answers. At the pre-registered 2.0 s reading a 1 s feed sits at the strategy's breakeven feed delay.

Impact is the measured live book of one day (2026-10-03, 9 WTA matches, 265 points with a >= 3c move), scaled down to smaller matches and never up (except in the depth sensitivity). Every fill is capped at the shares that were resting; depth on other days, at other tournaments or after we start trading may differ, and the fast tier may react to us (phi fixed).
How we share the stale depth with the fast tier is not known; the best-levels and pro-rata allocations bracket it and every capacity number is given for both.

Capital uses the repo's 4 h ex-ante lock. Locking each position until its market closes (payout available) needs about the same capital (section 3); a few percent of fills sit in markets that close more than a day later.
v2 has no price-impact model: it never fills beyond the print it copies, so its larger rows are upper bounds; phi_v2 < 1 is the only competition dial.
The burned OOS is non-blind (looked at before); it is reported, never used to choose a size. Seed bands are model draws, not data uncertainty.
The volume trend is a log-linear fit to one venue's tennis tapes, descriptive only; per-match volume has been flat, so the depth-growth cells are a sensitivity with no date attached.
The camera-free cost assumes a licensed betting-video feed costs the same as the point-data licence (no public price) and uses the L4 GPU price; T4 throughput at 120 fps is not measured.
The end-to-end timing run's 100-share probes on pre-match books are not capacity evidence; they were bound by the net cap on deep, quiet books.
